name: DAAD Scholarships for International Students
description: The German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) provides fully funded scholarships for international students, graduates, and researchers to study at German universities. Non-EU nationals and refugees receive a monthly stipend of €992 for master's students and €1,350 for doctoral candidates, plus health insurance coverage, travel allowance, and tuition fee waivers at public universities. DAAD is one of the world's largest funding organizations for international academic exchange, supporting over 100,000 students and researchers each year. Programs range from short-term research stays to full degree scholarships, with special tracks for students from developing countries and conflict-affected regions.
eligibility: International students and researchers from all countries; specific programs target students from developing countries and refugees; applicants must hold a bachelor's degree (for master's programs) or master's degree (for doctoral programs); German or English language proficiency required depending on program
amount: €992/month (master's), €1,350/month (doctoral) plus health insurance, travel allowance, and tuition waiver
applicationProcess: Apply through the DAAD scholarship database (daad.de/en/study-and-research-in-germany/scholarships/) by selecting the appropriate program. Most programs require an online application through the DAAD portal with supporting documents. Application deadlines are typically between October and February for the following academic year. Some programs require nomination by a DAAD partner institution in the applicant's home country.
geographicScope: Germany — all German public and participating private universities
documentsRequired: Bachelor's or master's degree certificate and transcripts, CV, letter of motivation, two academic reference letters, proof of language proficiency (German or English), research proposal (for doctoral programs), valid passport

name: Esperanza Education Fund Scholarship
description: The Esperanza Education Fund awards scholarships of $5,000 to $20,000 to students born outside the United States who are pursuing higher education at accredited U.S. colleges and universities. The fund supports first-generation college students and immigrants who demonstrate academic achievement, leadership potential, and financial need. Esperanza specifically targets immigrant students who may face barriers to accessing traditional financial aid, including undocumented students and DACA recipients. The scholarship can be applied toward tuition, fees, books, and living expenses at both undergraduate and graduate levels.
eligibility: Students born outside the United States who are enrolled or accepted at an accredited U.S. college or university; must demonstrate financial need and academic achievement; open to undocumented students and DACA recipients; first-generation college students preferred
applicationProcess: Submit an online application through the scholarship portal. Applications typically open in the fall semester and close in the spring. Applicants must complete a personal essay describing their immigrant experience and educational goals, provide academic transcripts, and submit letters of recommendation.
geographicScope: United States — accredited colleges and universities nationwide
documentsRequired: Academic transcripts, personal essay, two letters of recommendation, proof of enrollment or acceptance at a U.S. college/university, financial need documentation

name: MALDEF Scholarship Resource Guide 2026–2027
organization: Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund (MALDEF)
description: The MALDEF Scholarship Resource Guide is a comprehensive directory of scholarships available to Latino and immigrant students in the United States for the 2026–2027 academic year. Updated annually, the guide lists hundreds of scholarships from private foundations, corporations, universities, and government programs that are accessible to immigrant students regardless of immigration status. MALDEF compiles this resource specifically to help immigrant and Latino families navigate the complex landscape of educational funding, including scholarships that do not require U.S. citizenship or permanent residency. The guide covers undergraduate, graduate, and professional degree programs.
eligibility: Latino and immigrant students in the United States; includes scholarships open to undocumented students and DACA recipients; covers all levels from high school seniors to graduate students
amount: Varies by scholarship (directory lists hundreds of individual opportunities)
applicationProcess: Access the free guide on the MALDEF website. The guide provides direct links and instructions for each listed scholarship. No application to MALDEF itself is required — applicants apply directly to individual scholarship programs listed in the guide.
documentsRequired: Varies by individual scholarship; the guide specifies requirements for each listing

name: Global Impact Initiative — Accelerated ESL Program for Refugees
description: The Global Impact Initiative provides intensive, fully funded online English as a Second Language (ESL) instruction to adult refugee students residing in the United States. The program is designed to accelerate English proficiency for refugees who need language skills to access employment, education, healthcare, and community integration. All coursework, materials, and instruction are offered completely free of charge through scholarships, partnerships, and grant funding. The curriculum covers practical English for daily life, workplace communication, and academic preparation, with flexible scheduling to accommodate working adults and parents.
eligibility: Adult refugees residing in the United States; free of charge regardless of immigration status; priority given to refugees with limited English proficiency who are seeking employment or further education
amount: Free (fully funded through scholarships and grants — no cost to participants)
applicationProcess: Register through the Global Impact Initiative website. Students are enrolled on a rolling basis as space becomes available. An initial language assessment determines placement level. No formal documentation of refugee status is required at enrollment.
geographicScope: United States — online program accessible nationwide
documentsRequired: No formal documents required for enrollment; proof of identity helpful but not mandatory

name: New York Office for New Americans — English Language Programs
organization: New York State Department of State — Office for New Americans
description: The New York State Office for New Americans (ONA) funds and coordinates English language learning programs across New York State to help immigrants achieve language proficiency. Supported with approximately $1.29 million through Federal Community Service Block Grant funding, ONA partners with community organizations, libraries, and educational institutions to deliver free English classes at multiple proficiency levels. Programs include in-person and virtual ESL classes, citizenship preparation courses with English components, workforce-oriented English training, and multilingual resource navigation. ONA operates 27 Opportunity Centers statewide providing direct language services and referrals.
eligibility: Immigrants, refugees, asylees, and foreign-born residents of New York State regardless of immigration status; services are free and open to all proficiency levels
amount: Free services (funded by $1.29M Federal Community Service Block Grant)
applicationProcess: Visit any of the 27 ONA Opportunity Centers across New York State or call the ONA hotline at 1-800-566-7636 for referral to the nearest English language program. Walk-ins are accepted at most locations. Online registration available for virtual classes through partner organizations.
geographicScope: New York State — 27 Opportunity Centers statewide including New York City, Long Island, Hudson Valley, Capital Region, and Western New York
documentsRequired: No documents required for enrollment in most programs; photo ID helpful but not mandatory; no proof of immigration status required

name: EDU_MIG — Erasmus Mundus Master in Education, Migration, and Diversity
description: EDU_MIG is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degree program focused on Education, Migration, and Diversity, funded by the European Union. Students study across at least two European universities, earning a joint or multiple degree in a field directly relevant to migration and integration. The scholarship covers full tuition fees, a monthly living allowance of €1,400, comprehensive health insurance, travel costs, and installation costs. The program trains professionals to work in education policy, refugee integration, multicultural education, and migration governance. EDU_MIG specifically recruits students from refugee backgrounds and developing countries.
eligibility: International students holding a bachelor's degree; students from refugee backgrounds and developing countries receive priority for Erasmus Mundus scholarships; applicants must demonstrate interest in education, migration, or diversity studies; English language proficiency required (minimum B2 CEFR)
amount: Full tuition + €1,400/month living allowance + health insurance + travel costs (approximately €49,000 total for the 2-year program)
applicationProcess: Apply through the EDU_MIG consortium website (edumig.org) during the annual application window, typically October through January. Submit an online application with all supporting documents. Candidates are evaluated based on academic merit, motivation, and relevance of background. Shortlisted candidates may be interviewed.
geographicScope: Europe — consortium universities in at least two EU countries
documentsRequired: Bachelor's degree certificate and transcripts, CV, letter of motivation, two academic reference letters, proof of English proficiency (IELTS 6.5+ or equivalent), valid passport, portfolio of relevant work or research (if applicable)
